question: Does sign-pattern matching between query and context embeddings (binary overlap score) provide a fast pre-filtering mechanism that maintains recall@10 ≥85% while reducing candidate set by ≥60%?
why_matters: Two-stage retrieval (fast binary pre-filter → precise full-embedding rerank) could reduce computational cost on mobile devices
Paper shows sign overlap correlates with generalization; high sign agreement between query-context may predict retrieval relevance
Reducing candidate pool from 1,325 to ~530 items before expensive semantic scoring could improve overall latency by 2-3x
hypotheses: H1: Binary pre-filter achieves recall@10 ≥85% when retrieving top-100 candidates (vs full corpus)
H2: Combined two-stage pipeline (binary filter → semantic rerank) maintains final recall@3 ≥60.0% (current: 61.4%)
H3: End-to-end retrieval latency improves by ≥40% compared to single-stage semantic search
setup: Extend PoC 007 harness with two-stage retrieval: (1) Binarize EmbeddingGemma vectors using sign(), (2) Stage 1: compute Hamming distance between query and all document chunks, select top-K candidates (test K=50,100,200), (3) Stage 2: run full semantic search only on candidates, apply hybrid weighting (0.7 semantic + 0.3 BM25), (4) Measure recall@3, recall@10 after stage 1, end-to-end latency. Baseline: PoC 007 single-stage retrieval.
decision_rule: If H1 (recall@10 ≥85%) AND H2 (recall@3 ≥60%) AND H3 (latency improvement ≥40%): adopt; if H2 fails (recall@3 <59%): reject; if only H3 fails: inconclusive (latency not critical for current use case)
source_title: The Sign Code: The Hidden Binary Nature of Deep Networks

gate1.reason: This idea directly addresses established latency and computational constraints on mobile devices through a two-stage retrieval architecture. It proposes a concrete tradeoff between computational cost (binary pre-filtering) and quality (maintaining recall thresholds), with specific measurable success criteria: ≥85% recall@10 for pre-filter, ≥60% final recall@3, and ≥40% latency improvement. All hypotheses are testable with existing CUAD dataset and baseline metrics from PoC 007-009.

gate2.reason: The core mechanism is well-understood (sign-based binarization creates a fast approximate nearest neighbor filter using Hamming distance). Implementation path is clear with specific tools (numpy sign(), scipy Hamming distance, existing PoC 007 harness). We can predict speedup from reduced candidates but recall degradation is less certain without understanding embedding structure.

gate3.reason: This is an excellent pre-filtering PoC with minimal resource overhead (sign bits are extremely compact), clear fail-fast validation (can test recall in day 1-2), and strong fit for on-device constraints. The binary nature makes it ideal for iPhone deployment with negligible memory/compute impact.
